passages.title: The quiet hour
passages.content:
A university library introduced a quiet hour each afternoon. During that hour, group discussions moved to a separate room, while the main reading hall remained open for individual work. Some students initially worried that the change would reduce opportunities to collaborate. After a month, however, they reported that a clear division of spaces made both activities easier.

The librarians did not assume that silence alone would improve learning. They invited students to explain how they used the building and adjusted the timetable after collecting comments. The experiment suggests that a useful study environment depends on listening to its users as well as setting rules.

passages.title: Repair before replacement
passages.content:
A small college opened a repair workshop where students could bring damaged household objects. Volunteers taught visitors how to identify simple faults before deciding whether an item needed replacing. The workshop was free, but visitors were asked to describe what they had learned so that future volunteers could benefit.

Not every object could be repaired safely. Electrical equipment with exposed wiring was referred to qualified technicians. The organisers considered recognising these limits an essential part of the project. Their aim was to encourage thoughtful decisions about resources, rather than to promise that every broken object could be saved.

papers.writingPrompt: Write an essay discussing how a university can provide better spaces for independent study and collaboration.
papers.writingInstructions: Original functional sample, not a CET-6 exam task. Write 150–200 words and support your view with examples.
papers.chineseText: 这所大学的图书馆为学生提供安静的阅读空间，也为小组讨论设置了独立的房间。图书管理员定期收集学生的意见，并根据实际需要调整开放时间。
papers.referenceTranslation: The university library provides quiet reading spaces as well as separate rooms for group discussions. Librarians regularly collect students’ comments and adjust opening hours according to their needs.
